section: Objectives of Indian planning; types of planning (imperative, indicative, perspective, rolling)
subsections: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal
Growth model → plan based on it
Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions
Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components

accepted.s: At which level is the District Planning Committee (DPC) associated with multi-level planning in India?
accepted.x: The District Planning Committee operates at the district level. State Planning Boards, block or mandal bodies, and Gram Panchayats function at the other indicated levels.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative level associated with the planning institution.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the institutional arrangement of multi-level planning?
o: Centre—NITI Aayog; State—Planning Boards; District—DPC; Block/Village—GPDP
Centre—DPC; State—NITI Aayog; District—GPDP; Block—Planning Commission
Centre—Planning Boards; State—DPC; District—GPDP; Block—NITI Aayog
Centre—GPDP; State—DPC; District—Planning Commission; Block—Planning Boards
accepted.x: Multi-level planning operates through NITI Aayog at the Centre, Planning Boards in the States, DPCs at the district level, and block or mandal bodies with Gram Panchayats through GPDPs.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate swapped authorities.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: The principal objective of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) is to:
o: Prepare plans based on local needs from the grassroots level
Replace State Planning Boards with Gram Panchayats
Impose uniform national targets on all villages
Transfer all district functions to the Union Government
accepted.x: GPDPs are intended to promote bottom-up planning by incorporating local needs and priorities into development plans.
accepted.tq: Apply the bottom-up planning principle to a local-government situation.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: Who flagged the growing centralisation of planning in 1961?
accepted.x: The JP Narayan Committee drew attention to the increasing centralisation of planning in 1961.
accepted.tq: Test the committee associated with a specific criticism and year.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consisted of programmes that operated outside the panchayats?
o: GPDP, DPC, NITI Aayog and SFDA
DPAP, NDC, IADP and Planning Boards
accepted.x: The Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA), Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP), Integrated Tribal Development Programme (ITDP) and Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) operated outside the panchayat framework.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete list rather than a partially familiar combination.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments are significant in the context of planning because they:
o: Made NITI Aayog a constitutional body
Restored the role of local bodies in development planning
accepted.x: The 73rd and 74th Amendments strengthened and restored the role of rural and urban local bodies in local development planning.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional reform to its planning consequence.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the NITI Aayog State Support Mission:
1. It helps States establish State Institutions for Transformation.
2. It can support the strengthening of Planning Boards.
3. It is associated with bottom-up institutional planning support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The State Support Mission supports States in establishing State Institutions for Transformation, strengthening Planning Boards and improving bottom-up planning institutions.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying each institutional function.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: The NITI Aayog-assisted Visakhapatnam Economic Region in Andhra Pradesh comprises how many districts?
accepted.x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region comprises 10 districts.
accepted.tq: Test the numerical composition of a regional planning unit.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the three Economic Regions of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Visakhapatnam—10 districts; Amaravati—9 districts; Tirupati—10 districts
Visakhapatnam—10 districts; Amaravati—10 districts; Tirupati—9 districts
Visakhapatnam—9 districts; Amaravati—10 districts; Tirupati—10 districts
Visakhapatnam—9 districts; Amaravati—9 districts; Tirupati—10 districts
accepted.x: The Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati Economic Regions comprise 10, 9 and 10 districts respectively.
accepted.tq: Split the options by comparing the numerical rows of the regional table.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region was launched on:
accepted.x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region was launched on 13 November 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish close dates by matching the event with its exact launch date.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region has an indicative target of achieving an economy of approximately:
accepted.x: The target associated with the Visakhapatnam Economic Region is approximately USD 750–800 billion by 2047.
accepted.tq: Use the exact range rather than a rounded or exaggerated substitute.
accepted.sec: Multi-level planning - centre, state, district, block, bottom-up goal

accepted.s: Who formulated the Visvesvaraya Plan of 1934?
accepted.x: M. Visvesvaraya formulated the Visvesvaraya Plan in 1934 and is regarded as the Father of Indian Planning.
accepted.tq: Match the plan with its proponent rather than its central idea.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which plan proposed doubling national income within a decade through industrialisation?
accepted.x: The Visvesvaraya Plan was the first blueprint and proposed industrialisation with the objective of doubling national income in a decade.
accepted.tq: Identify a plan from its distinctive numerical objective.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Bombay Plan of 1944–45 was prepared by:
accepted.x: The Bombay Plan, titled A Plan of Economic Development for India, was prepared by eight Bombay industrialists.
accepted.tq: Test the authorship of a named economic plan.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a central feature of the Bombay Plan?
o: A significant role for the State
accepted.x: The Bombay Plan favoured a significant State role, public sector development and protection of infant industries; it did not advocate a completely non-interventionist State.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the plan's stated policy orientation.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the Gandhian Plan?
o: Heavy industries, import substitution and dominant public sector
Agriculture, cottage industries and self-contained villages
Marxist socialism, consumer goods and centralised production
Urban facilities in rural clusters and metropolitan growth
accepted.x: The Gandhian Plan emphasised agriculture, cottage and village industries, and self-contained villages.
accepted.tq: Match the plan with its core idea, not merely its author.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the principles associated with the Gandhian Plan?
accepted.x: Swadeshi, Sarvodaya and Trusteeship were principles associated with the Gandhian Plan. It favoured a decentralised economic structure rather than centralised economic control.
accepted.tq: Use the ideological mismatch to identify the excluded principle.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who proposed the People's Plan of 1945?
accepted.x: M.N. Roy proposed the People's Plan in 1945.
accepted.tq: Directly test the proponent of a named plan.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The People's Plan was primarily influenced by:
accepted.x: The People's Plan was based on Marxist socialism and stressed basic necessities, agriculture and consumer goods.
accepted.tq: Identify the ideological foundation from the plan's core description.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The slogan ‘economic reforms with a human face’ is considered to echo the emphasis of the:
accepted.x: The 1990s slogan ‘economic reforms with a human face’ echoed the People's Plan's concern with basic necessities and welfare.
accepted.tq: Connect a later policy slogan with the plan whose social emphasis it reflects.
accepted.sec: Plan models → proponent  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which growth model was associated with the Third Five-Year Plan?
o: John Sandy and S. Chakravarty model
accepted.x: The Third Five-Year Plan, covering 1961–66, was associated with the John Sandy and S. Chakravarty model, known as the Gadgil Yojana model.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among close plan-model pairings using the plan sequence.
accepted.sec: Growth model → plan based on it  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following plans in chronological order of their periods:
A. Fourth Plan
B. Second Plan
C. Fifth Plan
D. First Plan
accepted.x: The First, Second, Fourth and Fifth Plans covered 1951–56, 1956–61, 1969–74 and 1974–79 respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last plan periods, then place the intervening plans.
accepted.sec: Growth model → plan based on it  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Allen S. Manne and Ashok Rudra model was associated with the:
accepted.x: The Allen S. Manne and Ashok Rudra model was associated with the Fourth Five-Year Plan, 1969–74.
accepted.tq: Test the less frequently recalled model-plan association directly.
accepted.sec: Growth model → plan based on it  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Dhar model was associated with the Fifth Plan. The John W. Miller model was associated with the Eighth Plan, while Harrod-Domar and Feldman-Mahalanobis were associated with the First and Second Plans respectively.
accepted.tq: Eliminate swapped model-plan pairings by fixing the sure association.
accepted.sec: Growth model → plan based on it  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The wage goods model of C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda stressed:
o: Only heavy capital goods and steel production
Complete replacement of agriculture by industry
accepted.x: The wage goods model was an alternative to the Mahalanobis approach and stressed wage goods such as food and consumer goods together with employment.
accepted.tq: Contrast an alternative model with the heavy-industry emphasis of another model.
accepted.sec: Growth model → plan based on it  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Planning Commission was created by:
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was created by an executive resolution and was neither a constitutional nor a statutory body.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal basis and reject constitutional-status traps.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the National Development Council?
o: It is a judicial body that audits plan expenditure.
It is an extra-constitutional apex body that finally approves Five-Year Plans.
It is a statutory body that appoints the Deputy Chairman of NITI Aayog.
It is a constitutional body that prepares the Union Budget.
accepted.x: The NDC was an extra-constitutional apex body and had the function of finally approving Five-Year Plans.
accepted.tq: Use status and principal function together to identify the correct institution.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following persons or groups formed part of the National Development Council?
o: Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers, Union Territory representatives and Planning Commission members
accepted.x: The NDC included Union Cabinet Ministers, all Chief Ministers, representatives of Union Territories and members of the Planning Commission.
accepted.tq: Test institutional composition by rejecting the word ‘only’.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Planning Commission:
1. It assessed available resources.
2. It formulated Five-Year Plans.
3. It fixed priorities and allocated resources.
4. It appraised progress and planned grants to States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four were functions of the Planning Commission: resource assessment, plan formulation, priority-setting, resource allocation, progress appraisal and planning grants to States.
accepted.tq: Verify each listed function before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best distinguishes NITI Aayog from the former Planning Commission?
o: NITI Aayog is a constitutional body whereas the Planning Commission was statutory.
NITI Aayog is a fund allocator and the Planning Commission was only a think tank.
NITI Aayog prepares the Union Budget in place of the Finance Ministry.
NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up and cooperative federalism and functions as a think tank rather than a fund allocator.
accepted.x: NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism and functions primarily as a think tank, not as a fund allocator.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-role trap to distinguish two successor institutions.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the National Development Council is correct after the creation of NITI Aayog?
o: It was converted into a statutory tribunal.
It was abolished by a constitutional amendment on 1 January 2015.
It became the fund-allocating arm of NITI Aayog.
accepted.x: A formal resolution abolishing the National Development Council remains pending; replacement of the Planning Commission did not itself complete that formal abolition.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between practical discontinuation and formal abolition.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission and NDC - set-up, status, chairman, functions  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which sector was emphasised in the Mahalanobis strategy?
o: Consumer goods produced exclusively by large private firms
accepted.x: The Mahalanobis strategy emphasised basic and heavy capital-goods industries such as steel and machinery.
accepted.tq: Identify the central emphasis of the strategy from its sectoral choices.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mahalanobis strategy?
accepted.x: The strategy emphasised import substitution, self-reliance and a dominant public sector. Exports and export promotion were neglected rather than depended upon.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed policy orientation in an excluded component.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Mahalanobis strategy assumed the economy to be:
accepted.x: The strategy assumed a closed economy, which contributed to the neglect of foreign trade and export promotion.
accepted.tq: Infer the treatment of foreign trade from the strategy's policy assumptions.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Mahalanobis strategy, consumer goods were largely left to the:
accepted.x: Consumer goods were largely left to the small and cottage sector, while the public sector concentrated on basic and heavy industries.
accepted.tq: Contrast the sector assigned to consumer goods with the heavy-industry sector.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Mahalanobis strategy sought to raise the investment rate from:
accepted.x: The strategy aimed to raise investment from 7 per cent to 11 per cent of national income.
accepted.tq: Test both endpoints of the investment-rate target.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of steel plants is associated with the Second Plan?
accepted.x: The Second Plan included the development of steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct industrial-project pair from the plan period.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which industrial establishments were associated with the Second Plan besides the major steel plants?
o: Cochin Shipyard and Salem Steel Plant
Chittaranjan locomotives and Perambur coach factory
accepted.x: The Second Plan was also associated with Chittaranjan locomotive production and the Perambur coach factory.
accepted.tq: Use the industrial-project association to distinguish the Second Plan.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The growth target and achievement of the Second Plan were approximately:
accepted.x: The Second Plan had a growth target of 4.5 per cent and achieved approximately 4.21 per cent.
accepted.tq: Keep target and achievement in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components

accepted.s: The Mahalanobis strategy is often described as a strategy of:
o: Balanced growth based equally on all sectors
Unbalanced growth centred on heavy industry
accepted.x: The strategy is described as unbalanced growth because it gave priority to basic and heavy industries while neglecting agriculture, exports and consumer goods.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison between included and neglected sectors to identify the strategy's character.
accepted.sec: Mahalanobis strategy - included and excluded components
